title: Prefill/decode prioritizer using attention-sparsity signals
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency for workloads where attention sparsity materially reduces kernel execution cost by prioritizing prefill and short-decode requests that benefit from sparse kernels, while preserving tenant fairness and overall throughput. Background: Our runtime now exposes a compact attention-sparsity estimator (sparsity_score in [0,1]) and a fast kernel-cost predictor for a handful of kernel variants. Current schedulers treat requests primarily by token-count and tenant credits; they miss cases where a long sequence with high sparsity is cheaper than a short dense request. Proposal: Implement a lightweight prioritizer that computes a request-level "efficiency_score" = f(sparsity_score, predicted_kernel_cost, remaining_tokens, tenant_priority_credit). The scheduler uses efficiency_score to: - Prefer early placement of prefill or decode work that unlocks cheap sparse-kernel execution paths (soft fast-path). - Apply proportional fairness by scaling efficiency_score with tenant_credit_factor to avoid starvation. - Soft-demote requests expected to cause heavy dense kernels during hedging windows. Implementation plan: 1) Add an efficiency_score API on request metadata in the router (safe default = size-based score when signals missing). 2) Integrate kernel-cost probe: sample 1% of in-flight requests to validate predicted cost vs observed. 3) Scheduler patch: scoring-based queue ordering with a conservative headroom guard to preserve latency SLOs. 4) Offline simulation using 14 days of production traces (stable + spike periods) and microbenchmarks for sparse/dense kernels. Metrics and acceptance criteria: - Prefill 95/99 tail latency reduction >= 15% on sparsity-heavy workloads. - Overall token throughput change <= -5% (no more than 5% throughput regression). - Tenant fairness: 95th percentile tenant slowdown <= 1.2x relative to baseline. - No increase in error/fallback rate > 0.5%. Rollout plan: feature gate default off -> ramp 5% (canary), 20%, 50%, 100% with real-time dashboards. Risk / trade-offs: - Mis-estimated sparsity could cause suboptimal kernel selection and oscillation; mitigated with sampled kernel probe and damping factor. - Extra scheduling overhead must be <1% CPU of router; use simple arithmetic for score. Notes: This is intentionally orthogonal to heavier phase-splitting work; it augments split policies by providing a cost signal to inform where splits yield most benefit.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Triage: Added initial concept sketch and prioritized as P1. PM asked for concrete acceptance metrics.
2026-02-18 - Design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/attn-sparsity-prioritizer. Includes efficiency_score formula variants and simulation plan.
2026-02-25 - Engineering sync: Decided to implement conservative default (score falls back to token-length when estimator missing). Action: add kernel-cost probe and router hook.

2026-03-03 - Prototype results (local replay): On a synthetic sparse-heavy trace prefill 99th reduced from 420ms -> 330ms (approx 21% improvement). Throughput measured -2.8% across the run. Observed a small fairness blip for one low-credit tenant; added tenant_credit_floor to prevent demotion below baseline.

2026-03-05 - PR opened for router scoring and probe collector: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4210. Comments from Diego Marquez (PM): request clearer rollback path and metrics in dashboard. Megan Lin (Design): confirm UX for feature flag in Console.

2026-03-07 - Added sampled kernel probe (1% default) and dashboard panels for predicted vs observed kernel time. Early probe shows model-family A average predicted/observed ratio ~1.05 (within tolerance).
2026-03-10 - Integration test: Canary replay on staging 5% traffic. No increased error rate. Next: run 14-day production trace simulation and prepare A/B canary for next cycle.
Next steps: finalize scoring weights, add per-tenant tuning knobs, and schedule canary rollout with SRE on 2026-03-15.
